[\+ Follow](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=%2Fpulse%2Fdesigning-better-404-page-tips-structure-ideas-work-leetio-1pqwf&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_publisher-author-card)

A well-built 404 page helps reduce drop-offs, supports SEO, and keeps visitors engaged by guiding them to relevant content. This article explains what makes an effective 404 page, what to avoid, and how to design one that works. 👇

### Why are 404 pages important?

A 404 page is often the first thing users see when something on your site doesn't work as expected. If overlooked, you risk losing potential customers and damaging SEO performance.

Here’s what it contributes:

🔹 Reduce bounce rates: Users landing on an error page without a clear next step often leave immediately. Giving them links to the homepage, search, or relevant pages helps them stay on your site.

🔹 Support user experience: Clean visuals, consistent branding, and a helpful message can reduce frustration and keep users engaged.

🔹 Protect SEO performance: A well-configured 404 page prevents search engines from indexing broken links or irrelevant redirects, keeping your crawl budget focused.

🔹 Reveal weak points: Tracking 404 hits gives insight into broken internal links, outdated content, or bad backlinks that need fixing.

### What makes a good 404 page?

A well-built 404 page keeps users engaged, reduces bounce rates, and strengthens trust. A well-planned structure can even turn a lost click into a conversion opportunity.

✅ Clear communication: Let users know what happened in plain and friendly language. Avoid phrases like “HTTP 404 Not Found” or generic “Oops!” messages that say nothing useful. A simple message like “This page isn’t available” or “Looks like the link is broken” keeps things human and understandable.

✅ Consistent branding: The page should match the rest of your site visually and tonally. Stick to your usual fonts, color schemes, and voice. That consistency reinforces trust and reminds users they haven’t been kicked to a different site.

✅ Helpful navigation: Always give users somewhere to go next. Add links to the homepage, product catalog, latest blog post, or include a search bar. The faster people find something useful, the more likely they will stay.

✅ A touch of personality: A bit of humor or creativity (if aligned with your brand) can make the page more memorable and reduce user frustration. Just don’t let the design get in the way of usability.

✅ Calls to action or extra support: Use the space to offer something helpful: a newsletter signup, a contact button, or links to popular articles. For product-focused pages, highlighting a best-seller can keep interest alive.

✅ Considers accessibility: Make sure your 404 page works for all users. Keep the content screen-reader friendly, ensure readable contrast ratios, and use buttons that can be navigated with a keyboard. A smooth user experience means everyone can find their way back.

### Don’ts for 404 pages

Some mistakes make a 404 page more frustrating than helpful. If users land on an error page without context or guidance, they’ll likely exit the site and continue elsewhere. Here's what to avoid:

🔻 No message: A blank screen or raw server error gives users no clue what happened. For example, a plain “404 Not Found” without context or guidance creates confusion and damages trust.

🔻 Overloaded visuals or gimmicks: A funny animation might catch the eye, but if it overwhelms the page or distracts from navigation, it works against you. A flashy, interactive element with no links or explanation might entertain, but it won’t help someone trying to get back on track.

🔻 No return path: Missing links to the homepage, site menu, or search bar turn the page into a dead end. If users can’t navigate anywhere else, they’ll bounce. This is especially risky for e-commerce, where lost traffic means lost revenue.

🔻 Inconsistent branding: A generic or off-brand page can feel like a separate website. That disconnect increases the chance of users leaving. For instance, a corporate SaaS site with a 404 page full of unrelated stock images and casual slang risks confusing or alienating visitors.

🔻 Technical jargon: Error messages like “HTTP 404 - Not Found” without explanation aren’t helpful. Instead of tech lingo, say something like, “This page doesn’t exist anymore” or The link you followed might be outdated” paired with a way to get back on track.

### Best examples of 404 page

### 1\. Pixar

Pixar’s 404 page uses the character Sadness from Inside Out to soften the blow of a broken link. It's emotional and relatable and directly taps into the company’s storytelling roots.

https://www.pixar.com/404

### 2\. Marvel

Marvel’s 404 page uses a simple but clever reference to Thor’s hammer, with the line “You are not worthy”. It ties into the Marvel Universe and entertains fans with an inside joke while the design stays minimal and clean.

https://www.marvel.com/comaics

### 3\. LEGO

LEGO’s 404 page shows a worried minifigure holding two unplugged power cords. The visual humor reflects LEGO’s playful personality and turns a technical error into a light-hearted moment. 

https://www.lego.com/en-us/service/buildinginstruc45tions/?locale=en-us

### 4\. Dropbox

Dropbox’s 404 page is minimalist and user-focused. Instead of visual overload, it offers a short, clear message explaining the error, along with helpful links that guide users back to the site.

https://www.dropbox.com/business/sol342utions/sales

### 5\. Airbnb

Airbnb's 404 page is minimalist and straightforward.

How to Create a Custom 404 Page in WordPress with Visual Composer

On Posted on [July 29, 2021October 4, 2021](https://visualcomposer.com/blog/how-to-create-a-404-page/) by [Nikola Puciriusa](https://visualcomposer.com/blog/author/nikola/) to [Tutorials](https://visualcomposer.com/blog/category/tutorials/)

# How to Create a Custom 404 Page in WordPress

In a perfect world, websites would never experience technical issues and links would always lead you to the intended pages.

Well, you can turn this problem into an opportunity, in this case, and we'll show you how.

**In this article, we discuss:**

*   What is a 404 Error Page
*   Best Approach to Creating a 404 Page
*   How to Create a 404 Page
*   Best 404 Page Plugins
*   Most Unique 404 Page Examples

## What is a 404 Error Page?

A 404 Page - also know as HTTP 404, 404 Not Found, 404, 404 Error, Page Not Found - is an error that occurs when a user is trying to reach a non-existent page.

**A 404 Error happens when:**

1.  **A user is typing a domain URL by hand and misspells**.
2.  **The page user is trying to reach a page that has been deleted, moved, or renamed** without redirecting the URL, but there are old or incorrect backlinks still circulating the net.
3.  **The website is down**, either due to overcapacity (more users coming to a page than the server can handle), under maintenance or crashed for some reason.

In case any of these events take place - visitors land on a 404 page. This is where you can make your website visitor experience better by making the page functional or even beneficial. Similar to landing pages - you can lead users to where you want from there.

Moreso, most likely you will never be able to find & fix all of the broken links, or be able to ensure that users never mistype anything. This is why 404 pages are so important.

## Best Approaches to Creating a 404 Page

Like with any error occurring on a website, there is a high chance that users will leave. Our mission is to make sure that the visitors return to the content pages and continue browsing.

**The best 404 page practices are:**

*   **Display an error message** that lets the user know that they have reached an unavailable page.
*   **Maintain the branding of your site**. Don't forget to add a logo and continue with the existing color palette and font styles as in the rest of the website.
*   **Add a link back to the home page**. Ensure that the user has a place to return or go to next and is not left hanging in an empty space.
*   **Add a search bar**. This helps the user to navigate to the place they had intended, and you can also add suggestions.
*   **Add a menu bar**. This can also help users to “return to safety” and find their way back to the content.
*   **Add links to social media**. It is always a good practice to add ways that users can get in touch with you.
*   **Use humor**. Astonish your visitors by leaving a little less room for formalities and more for a chance to enlighten their day. They will probably be surprised if they don't reach the standard error page anyway.

There are multiple integrable elements to make your 404 pages functional and stunning. Remember that all of the elements mentioned above are optional - it is up to you how simple or extensive you make it.

## Best 404 Page Plugins

In addition, some add-ons offer to do the work for you. 

**The best WordPress plugins for managing 404 pages are:**

*   A great multi-use plugin that allows to **avoid 404 page errors** when you move or delete content with their Redirect Manager tool is [Yoast SEO](https://wordpress.org/plugins/wordpress-seo/). While its main purpose is to keep track of keyword usage and optimize your site for search engines, it is a great redirection tool as well.
*   The most popular regular expression (regex) tool in the WordPress plugin repository is [Redirection](https://wordpress.org/plugins/redirection/). It helps to **keep track of 404 errors**, manage 301 redirections, and tidy up any loose ends your site may have.
*   URL Fixers might also come in handy. For example, [Link Fixer](https://wordpress.org/plugins/permalink-finder/) detects when WordPress cannot find a permalink. Before it generates a 404 error it locates posts with similar words. As a result, instead of issuing a 404 error, it most likely **redirects the user to the intended page**.

## How to Create a 404 Page with Visual Composer

Thanks to website builders and other handy tools, creating a 404 page becomes a piece of cake. And in this video, we explain the best way to do it (and the easiest).

In case you are looking for an even quicker way to set a 404 page - Visual Composer offers over 300 predefined template solutions that are customizable to fit your brand.

In the Visual Composer Hub, you will find different content elements and add-ons, and also templates. Look for the marketplace icon in the navigation bar.

![Visual Composer Hub - The element, template and add-on Cloud](wp-content/uploads/2021/07/visual-composer-website-builder.png)

In the search bar, type in what you are looking for (i.e. “404”) and select from either the free or premium templates, depending on the plan you've chosen.

![404 page templates in the Visual Composer Hub](wp-content/uploads/2021/07/404-templates-visual-composer.png)

Once you are done designing your 404 page, you need to save the template. In this video, we explain how you can manage your 404 pages:

## Best 404 Page Examples

Now that you have learned how to set up 404 pages with Visual Composer, we would like to give you some great examples of 404 pages.

### Keep it Simple

This 404 page by [CharlieShotMe](http://charlieshotme.com/) is super simple yet elegant and perfectly matches the feel of the whole website. Remember, that 404 pages are not intended to keep the user for a while and instead to lead them back to content.

![Simple 404 page example by CharlieShotMe](wp-content/uploads/2021/07/404-charlieshotme.png)

404 Page By CharlieShotMe

### Be Creative

This is a great example of a creative 404 page design by [Bocconcini](https://www.bocconcininy.com/). Straightforward yet entertaining. Will make the user less if not at all dissatisfied with the fact that they have reached a dead-end page.

![Creative 404 page example by Bocconcini](wp-content/uploads/2021/07/bocconcini-404.png)

404 Page by Bocconcini

### Make it Visually Appealing

While you can never go wrong with simple designs, you can also never make a mistake with beautiful imagery. This great page design by [MartiniTime](https://martinitime.be/) has bypassed creating a 404 page, by simply redirecting all path links straight to the main page. Which by the way, is a one-page site (commonly used for informative purposes).

![Visually Appealing 404 page example by MartiniTime](wp-content/uploads/2021/07/martini-404.png)

404 Page by MartiniTime
